questionText: An effective way of controlling inflation in a mixed economy is to
explanation: Inflation arises when too much money chases too few goods, so raising productivity increases the supply of goods and closes the gap. Reducing income tax would add to spending power and make matters worse.

questionText: One of the limitations of the production possibility curve (PPC) assumption is that there is

options.B: no recognition of preferred goods for countries

explanation: The PPC is drawn on the assumption that the state of technology is fixed, so it cannot show how technical progress expands what an economy can produce. In reality technology changes and shifts the whole curve outward.

questionText: A major disadvantage of the arithmetic mean is that it is

options.B: not suitable for further statistical analysis
options.C: cumbersome to determine the actual value

explanation: Because the mean uses every observation in its computation, one unusually large or small value drags it away from the centre of the distribution. This sensitivity to outliers is its main weakness.

questionText: Demand patterns are determined by the market on the basis of
explanation: Consumer sovereignty means the consumer's spending decisions dictate what the market produces. The pattern of demand in the market is therefore the collective expression of that sovereignty.

questionText: A consumer surplus measures the

options.A: benefits derived from consuming a cheap commodity
options.B: excess of total expenditure over total utility
options.C: difference between marginal utility and marginal cost
options.D: excess of marginal utility over price

explanation: Consumer surplus is the amount by which the satisfaction a buyer derives from a unit exceeds what he actually pays for it. Expressed at the margin, it is marginal utility minus price.

questionText: If the demand for one commodity excludes another, it is said to be
explanation: Competitive demand arises between substitutes: buying one, such as butter, means not buying the other, such as margarine. Complementary goods are demanded together, not in place of each other.

questionText: The median of an odd-numbered set of scores is the
explanation: After arranging the scores in order of size, the median is the value that divides the set into two equal halves. With an odd number of scores that is simply the middle one.

questionText: If demand increases without a change in supply, equilibrium price and quantity will
explanation: A rightward shift of the demand curve along an unchanged supply curve moves the intersection up the supply curve, so both the equilibrium price and the equilibrium quantity rise.

questionText: In the process of production, total output is at maximum when
explanation: Marginal product is the addition to total output from one more unit of the variable factor. Total product stops rising exactly when that addition falls to zero, so total output peaks where MP = 0.

questionText:

From the table above, the price elasticity of supply is
explanation: Elasticity of supply is the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price. Quantity rises by 60/60 = 100% while price rises by 1/1 = 100%, so the coefficient is 100 ÷ 100 = 1.

questionText: When a consumer is at equilibrium, the marginal rate of substitution of x for y is equal to the
explanation: Consumer equilibrium occurs where the indifference curve is tangential to the budget line. At that point the slope of the indifference curve, the MRS, equals the slope of the budget line, which is the price ratio Px/Py.

questionText: Minimum price legislation by government will
explanation: A minimum price is fixed above the equilibrium to protect producers. At that higher price buyers take less while sellers offer more, so the quantity demanded falls and an unsold surplus builds up.

questionText: Ranking is the method used in measuring
explanation: The ordinal approach holds that satisfaction cannot be counted in units but can be placed in order of preference. Cardinal utility, by contrast, assumes satisfaction can be measured numerically in utils.

questionText: If a firm is faced with an elastic supply curve, its revenue will

options.A: be supplied at a higher price
options.C: increase by more than the percentage increase in price

explanation: Elastic supply means quantity responds more than proportionately to price. Since revenue is price times quantity, a given percentage rise in price raises revenue by a larger percentage.

questionText: The optimal range of output for a perfectly competitive firm is where
explanation: The optimum or most efficient level of output is the one produced at the least cost per unit, that is at the minimum point of the average cost curve. In long-run perfect competition the firm is driven to exactly that point.

questionText: A firm will experience diseconomies of scale when

options.A: there are difficulties in coordinating production
options.B: there is shortage in labour supply
options.C: the size of market is small
options.D: there is an increase in the price of raw materials

explanation: Diseconomies of scale come from within the firm as it grows too large: management becomes unwieldy, decisions slow down and coordination costs rise, pushing average cost up. Raw material prices are an external cost, not a scale effect.

questionText: The law of variable proportions is applicable only
explanation: The law requires at least one factor to be fixed while another is varied, and that is the definition of the short run. In the long run every factor can be varied, which is the domain of returns to scale.

questionText: From the diagram above, the optimal point of production is
explanation: The straight line UT is the isocost, showing what the producer can afford, and curves I, II and III are isoquants. The best attainable output is where the isocost just touches the highest reachable isoquant, which is the point of tangency S. R lies on a higher curve but is unaffordable, and T lies on a lower one.

questionText: If real income increases while nominal income remains the same, it can be inferred that
explanation: Real income is nominal income adjusted for the price level. If the money figure is unchanged but it now buys more, the only explanation is that prices have fallen.

questionText: One of the characteristics of oligopoly is the availability of
explanation: Oligopoly is a market dominated by a small number of large sellers, each of whom must watch the reactions of the others. A single seller is monopoly and many sellers give perfect or monopolistic competition.

questionText: The average total cost when 20 units are produced is
explanation: Read up from 20 on the quantity axis to the ATC curve, then across to the price axis: the value is ₦15.00.

questionText: When 20 units of output is produced, TC will be
explanation: Total cost is average total cost multiplied by output. The diagram gives an ATC of ₦15 at 20 units, so TC = 15 × 20 = ₦300.

questionText: The profit of a monopolist can be eliminated where price equals
explanation: Abnormal profit is the excess of price over average cost. Forcing price down to average cost leaves the monopolist covering all costs including normal profit, with no supernormal profit remaining.

questionText: Bank consolidation policy in Nigeria is a measure to increase
explanation: The 2004-2005 consolidation exercise raised the minimum capital requirement to ₦25 billion, forcing banks to merge or recapitalise. Its purpose was to strengthen the capital base and so the stability of the banking system.

questionText: An increase in the circulation of money without a corresponding increase in output will lead to
explanation: More money chasing the same quantity of goods bids prices up. This is the classic demand-pull inflation described by the quantity theory of money.

questionText: In national income accounts, an item counted as part of government spending is
explanation: Government spending in the accounts covers payments made in exchange for goods and services, such as the salaries of civil servants. Pensions, scholarships and welfare payments are transfer payments and are excluded to avoid double counting.

questionText: If aggregate demand is lower than total output in an economy, national income will
explanation: When planned spending falls short of what is produced, stocks pile up unsold and firms respond by cutting output and laying off workers. National income therefore falls until it matches aggregate demand.

questionText: During the era of barter, money was generally in the form of
explanation: Before coinage, ordinary goods such as cowries, salt, cattle and manilas served as the medium of exchange. This is why the earliest form of money is called commodity money.

questionText: A country achieves economic development when there is

options.C: a sustained increase in per capita income
options.D: an even distribution of goods and services

explanation: Development is measured by a lasting rise in output per head, which is what actually improves living standards. A rise in total output alone can be swallowed up by population growth.

questionText: An indicator of growth in an economy over a period of time is the
explanation: Economic growth is measured by the change in gross domestic product valued at market prices from one period to the next. The GDP gap measures unused capacity and the deflator measures the price level, not growth.

questionText: A country embarks on deficit financing in order to
explanation: Deficit financing means deliberately spending beyond revenue and borrowing the difference, so as to inject demand and encourage investment and employment. It is an expansionary measure and would add to inflation rather than curb it.

questionText: The deflationary gap is defined by
explanation: To the right of the equilibrium point E the aggregate supply line lies above the aggregate demand line, so planned spending falls short of what the economy produces. That shortfall, marked K, is the deflationary gap.

questionText: What does X represent?
explanation: To the left of E the aggregate demand line lies above aggregate supply, so spending exceeds the output available at those income levels. That excess, marked X, is the inflationary gap.

questionText: The import-substitution strategy of industrialization is to encourage
explanation: Import substitution sets out to manufacture at home the goods a country has been buying abroad, so as to save foreign exchange and build local industry behind protective tariffs.

questionText: Upstream oil activities involve the
explanation: The upstream sector covers the search for and extraction of crude — exploration, drilling and production. Refining and marketing belong to the downstream sector.

questionText: Agricultural production in Nigeria is constrained by
explanation: Successive agricultural programmes have been well conceived on paper but poorly executed, with funds diverted and schemes abandoned. Demand for food is never the binding constraint.

questionText: The main function of the NNPC is to

options.A: oversee the development of the oil sector

explanation: The Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation holds the government's interest in the industry and supervises exploration, production, refining and marketing across the sector. Developing the oil-producing communities is the mandate of other agencies.

questionText: Investing heavily in the agricultural sector will lead to
explanation: The direct return on investment in farming is a larger harvest, which is what secures the nation's food supply and cuts the food import bill.

questionText: Industrial development in Nigeria can be encouraged through
explanation: Reliable power, good roads and functioning ports cut the cost of production for every firm at once. Without them, subsidies merely offset the losses that poor infrastructure creates.

questionText: The record of a country's transactions in international trade is her
explanation: The balance of payments is the complete statement of a country's dealings with the rest of the world. The current account, capital account and balance of trade are all parts of it.

questionText: The transfer of public shareholding in corporations to private enterprises is
explanation: Privatisation is the sale of government-held equity in an enterprise to private buyers. Commercialisation leaves ownership with the state but requires the enterprise to run on business lines.

questionText: A condition in which official and autonomous exchange rates coexist is
explanation: Two rates running side by side — one fixed by the authorities and one set in the open market — is a dual exchange rate. Nigeria has operated such an arrangement at several points.

questionText: In modern economies, the Malthusian theory of population is ineffective because of
explanation: Malthus could not foresee the advances in farming — improved seed, fertiliser and machinery — that have raised food output far faster than he thought possible. Technology, not the checks he predicted, is what falsified him.

questionText: Optimum population enables an economy to attain the highest level of
explanation: The optimum population is the size that, combined with the country's resources and technology, yields the greatest output per person. Any more or any fewer people lowers income per head.

questionText: A change from one industry to another by a worker is an example of
explanation: Horizontal mobility is movement between jobs at the same level, such as a driver leaving a bakery for a brewery. Vertical mobility is promotion to a higher grade and geographical mobility is movement between places.

questionText: The money paid per hour for work done is
explanation: A wage rate is payment calculated per unit of time worked or per unit produced, typically per hour. A salary is a fixed monthly or annual payment that does not vary with hours.

questionText: Trade takes place because of
explanation: Countries gain by specialising in what they produce at the lowest relative cost and exchanging for the rest. Ricardo's principle of comparative advantage is the basis of that gain from trade.

questionText: The World Trade Organization is responsible for

options.B: ensuring equal participation of countries in trade
options.D: minimizing obstacles to international trade and investment

explanation: The WTO administers the rules of world trade and works to reduce tariffs, quotas and other barriers between member countries. Stabilising oil prices is the work of OPEC.
